summary:
NASM: four plain white_terracotta marble cubes (y2..11, x2..85) alternating with three lower dark-glass bays in blackstone grids (roofs y9), a dark top slot in each cube, granite terraces and the Ad Astra steel spire at the north entrance; planes hang inside the lit glass.
NMAI: stacked curved sandstone tiers (ellipses, each overhanging or stepping back) banded in horizontal strata with an orange course, a deep cantilevered lobe over the east door, and a shallow dome to y16.
Around it: a pond, grandfather rocks and native planting. It reads by its silhouette and colour: a long pale box-and-glass rhythm beside a golden, layered cliff. NASM: four white_terracotta cubes alternating with three lower gray-glass bays (blackstone grid), entrance in the central bay, Ad Astra spire, aircraft and a rocket glowing inside.
NMAI: four stacked banded-sandstone elliptical tiers overhanging, east lobe over the entrance, shallow dome to y16, pond, boulders and meadow.

NASM shell: NASM shell built: four marble cubes (walls, roof deck, coping, plinth ring), podium y1 (granite edge, smooth_stone inside, bay face rows and G2 recess left free), clerestory slots. make.sh whole, no refusals; check clean apart from one orphan grass block at 77,0,29. Not rendered.
polish: Not rendered or fit-checked by eye
Terrace paving z 1..3 and G1/G3 z 4 north strips are for the grounds part
Bay face rows (z0/z1) and G2 recess z 4..5 left empty for glass part and entry steps

waste.what: Worked out which podium cells to skip around the bay faces by hand
waste.cost: one small loop, a few coordinates
waste.tool: a plan.md table of podium cells to leave free, or a podium(g, box, skipRects) helper

summary: NASM glass bays: ["NASM glass bays built in parts/nasm-glass.mjs: G1 x15..24, G2 x38..49 (mullions 38/41/46/49), G3 x63..72, roof glass, sills, transoms, mullions.", "G2 iron_door pairs at x42..45 y2..3 in the north (z6) and south (z24) faces, with a blackstone lintel at y4; entry_steps slab at z3 and landing z4..5 at y1.", "make.sh finishes: this part placed 1190 blocks with 0 refused and 0 off-palette; check reports no floating or unsupported blocks; fit OK; front elevation and front-left tiles show the glass bays and G2 doors."]
polish: The nasm-grounds worker should skip the G2 entrance row at z3 (x38..49), which this part's slab already holds; the grounds table also lists it.
No zoomed close-up of the G2 door hinges and the entrance steps was rendered; only the full elevation and the front-left iso were checked by eye.
The orphan grass_block at 77,0,29 comes from the ground layer, not from this part.
The south entrance has no steps or landing of its own in this part, per plan; the grounds part owns the south landing.

waste.what: Hand-chose the door_pair left/right x-origins for the north and south G2 faces, working out that a south-facing pair runs toward lower x
waste.cost: about 3 minutes of reasoning, one pass
waste.tool: door_pair could take the span (x0..x1) and set the pairs itself, or document the cell order for each facing

waste.what: Wrote the blackstone lintel at y4 over the doors cell by cell with g.set, since glass_bay fills those cells with glass first
waste.cost: 8 set() calls by hand
waste.tool: glass_bay opts.lintels or opts.openings that leaves the door cells to door_pair, or a helper that paints a frame over a glazed face

waste.what: Needed { over: true } on door_pair because glass_bay had already filled the door cells, so the call order (glass first, then doors) had to be learned by trial
waste.cost: one retry of the design
waste.tool: glass_bay opts.openings: a list of cells to leave as air, so doors and frames can be placed into air afterwards

waste.what: A sed -i without a backup suffix failed on macOS, so the elements.md tick needed a second attempt
waste.cost: one failed command
waste.tool: a plan-tick script (mcd tick <file> <id>) that edits checklists without sed

companions.task: Cut and lay the G2 entrance steps and landing (the z3 slab row and the z4..5 full-block landing) and check the half-step rise against the threshold.
Hang the iron door pairs in G2's north and south faces and check the hinge side and the open swing against the landing.
Walk the street-to-door approach for G2 with $MCD approach, confirming the half-step run, the 2-long landing and the level threshold.

summary: NASM fittings: ["NASM fittings built in parts/nasm-fittings.mjs: three aircraft hung in G1, G2 (two) and G3 on chains to the bay roofs, a standing rocket in G3, 32 pearlescent froglights on the bay floors, and the Ad Astra spire at x 35 z 2 (iron_block shaft y 2..13, lightning rod to 17, end_rod bursts at 11 and 13).", "make.sh writes a whole build.nbt with 216 fittings blocks, 0 refused. `mcd fit` reports OK. Zoom renders show the planes, rocket and spire reading correctly.", "Two deviations from plan.md, both noted there: the glow sits at y 2 (the shell fills the bay floor at y 1 and runParts locks it), and the planes' fins are cut down or dropped because the bay roof is at y 9."]
polish: Glow froglights are at y 2, not the plan's y 1 floor: the shell's smooth_stone at y 1 is locked. To sit them flush, the shell must leave those 32 cells air (plan.md Notes).
palette.json lists iron_chain, which is not a 1.21.1 id; the server id is `chain`. The helper writes `chain`, so the build reports 12 off-palette chains until palette.json is fixed.

`mcd check` shows the three aircraft as floating groups and the spire base as an orphan. Both clear once the glass part builds the y 9 roofs and the grounds part lays the y 1 Ad Astra terrace; not fixable in this part.
Fin height: G1 plane has a 1-high fin; G2 and G3 planes (body y 7) have none, because the bay roof is glass at y 9. Accepted, noted in plan.md.
Light: the froglights (level 15) cover the bay floors, but I did not run `mcd light` on the finished bays because the glass part isn't built yet.

waste.what: Converted each plan box (fuselage x/z corner, span, len, wing centre) into aircraft() spec numbers by hand, and worked out which fin and chain cells would hit the y 9 roof.
waste.cost: about 6 coordinate calculations and 2 corrections (fin height, jet orientation) after the first build
waste.tool: A `mcd` or build-library helper that takes a plan box for each aircraft (e.g. aircraft({box:[x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1], axis, hang})) and clamps the fin and hangers to the roof and to the room's ceiling.

waste.what: Checked the glow cells against the shell's face rows and interior z ranges by reading the shell source, instead of reading them off the grid.
waste.cost: one source read plus 32 cells listed by hand
waste.tool: A `mcd plan`-style query that prints each bay's interior cells at a given y, filtered by what earlier parts already placed (air-aware).

waste.what: Confirmed the chain id by hand with `mcd blocks --check` under two versions, after the default 26.3 check had given a misleading answer.
waste.cost: 3 tool calls
waste.tool: `mcd blocks --check` should default to the build's DataVersion (or the server version) rather than the latest release; palette.json should be checked against 1.21.1 automatically.

waste.what: Wrote the plan.md Notes and ticked elements.md by hand, and retried after a BSD sed `-i` mistake.
waste.cost: 2 tool calls
waste.tool: A checklist helper that ticks elements by ID and appends a dated note to plan.md Notes.

companions.task: Glass roof and bay walls at y 9 with the chain hanger points, so the aircraft and chains connect to real frame instead of floating in the check.
Check the bay floors' light level with `mcd light` after the glass part is in, and decide whether the froglight grid is enough for the bay interiors at dusk.
Proportions for the three hung aircraft (wing span to fuselage, tail fin height) so they read as the right types from the aerial view, with the fin room the y 9 roof allows.

summary:
NASM grounds: NASM grounds built in parts/nasm-grounds.mjs: granite terraces, forecourt edge slabs and side aprons at y 1 (only on '#' cells), south planter strips with a 1-high granite curb, azalea and short grass, and garden lamps in each planter.
Terrace lamp posts sit at z 2 and z 3 per RESERVED, plus lamps for the 1-wide west and east aprons. make.sh writes a whole build.nbt: NASM grounds 481 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette.
Checks: mcd check shows 0 floating and 0 unsupported; mcd fit is OK; renders read correctly. E7 and E11 ticked in elements.md, and a Notes line added to plan.md.
polish: Sealed cube interiors (x 2..14, 25..37, 50..62, 73..85, z 4..26) read light 0 on the light map. Mobs can spawn in a sealed hollow room, so the shell owner or a final lamp pass should light them or fill them.

The west and east aprons are dark outside the lamp spots. The 1-wide strip at x 1 z 20..24 is lit by the lamp at (1,2,20), but the east side of the lot still needs a check once the NMAI grounds are in.

The north strip has no paving at x 11..25 z 3, because the plot footprint has no ground there. The terrace has a gap between the west and Ad Astra terraces; that is the plot's real footprint, not an error.
G2 entry steps (x 38..49, z 3..5) are left to nasm-glass, and the plan has no checklist, so only elements.md E7 and E11 are ticked.

waste.what: Worked out each planter stub's curb, interior and lamp cell by hand from the footprint and ground maps, then rewrote the loop after the first light check showed the south strip dark.
waste.cost: about 3 edit/build cycles
waste.tool: a vocab planter helper that takes per-cell ground (g) from the site maps, with a lamp option, so curbs and plants follow the ground without the caller doing the arithmetic

waste.what: Read the light map as a text grid by eye to find dark strips and 1-wide aprons, then added lamps by trial.
waste.cost: 2 light runs and 1 rebuild
waste.tool: mcd light with a per-cell list of dark cells, or an option to suggest lamp spots for dark cells outside rooms (site-level version of mcd room's lantern spots)

waste.what: Ticked elements by hand and wrote a Notes line into plan.md.
waste.cost: 3 small edits
waste.tool: a script that ticks the elements.md checkbox for a part and appends its notes

companions.task: Take the outdoor light pass across the whole NASM lot: confirm every stub, apron and terrace is at light 8 or more, and place lamps only where the light map leaves dark cells.
Lay the granite paving and step edges (the z 1 slab row on the east forecourt, the G2 south landing) to match the plan's paving courses.

summary:
NMAI shell: parts/nmai-shell.mjs builds the NMAI shell: four strata tiers (T1 solid floor, T2..T4 open over the atrium), tier-top rings, solid east lobes with slab tops, ribbon slits on the south/west arcs, the dark oak east doors (two pairs) with porch lanterns, and the Potomac dome.
make.sh runs whole: NMAI shell places 2794 blocks with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines; $MCD check shows 0 floating and 0 unsupported; the only orphan is the intended T2 overhang lip at 111,5,19.
Not built: the cut_sandstone door-jamb frame and brown_stained_glass flanks in E15 (the T1 curve never reaches x125 at z6..7 or z12..13). Elements E12, E13, E14, E16, E17 ticked in elements.md; plan.md Notes has my deviations.
polish: E15 door frame and flanks not built: plan's brown_stained_glass flanks at x125..126 z6..7 / z12..13 sit outside T1's ellipse, so there is no wall cell there; the cut_sandstone jambs need a decision from the architect.
The tier-top ring inner ellipse is widened to 5.5 (plan says 5) so the dome's edge stairs sit on the drum course; the dome helper's drum is smaller than the plan's E(110,10,5,5) atrium.
Lobes are solid cantilevers (not hollow rings) built from the cells outside the tiers they touch; the plan's soffit wording only partly applies because the lobes sit on each other.
In the front-right iso tile the NMAI massing appears on the left (west) and NASM on the right; the grid coordinates follow plan.md, but this view orientation was not checked against the Mall layout.
Porch floor, boulders and lamps belong to the grounds parts; the dome's ochre_froglight at y15 is set by the potomac_dome helper and was not separately verified.

waste.what: Ran a full make.sh only to find tier_ring takes [cx, cz, rx, rz] arrays while the rest of the kit uses {cx, cz, rx, rz} objects; the helper's signature was learned by a crash, not by the spec.
waste.cost: 1 failed build, about 2 minutes
waste.tool: vocab helpers should accept both ellipse forms, or the spec should show a literal example call for each helper with its argument shape

waste.what: Found the dome-edge stairs standing on my tier-top slab (half a block of air) only through `mcd fit` after the build; the mismatch is between the dome helper's drum radius and the atrium ellipse I used.
waste.cost: 1 rebuild and a fit read, plus a manual ring-size guess
waste.tool: a dome/drum footprint export (the drum's cell list) that tier_ring can take as its inner ellipse, or a potomac_dome option that returns the cells it used

waste.what: Wrote the solid elliptical lobes by hand: cellsOf() plus nested loops, skip sets, and a separate loop for each slab top.
waste.cost: about 30 lines of loop code, 4 set calls per lobe course
waste.tool: a shape brush `solidEllipse(g, E, {y0, y1, skip: [E...], material: strata})` and a `topSlab` helper that caps the exposed top of a solid mass

waste.what: Carved the door cells (x125, y2..3, z8..11) by hand before door_pair, because tier() fills the wall and door_pair refuses non-air cells.
waste.cost: one carve call; had to work out the order
waste.tool: door_pair or tier option `openings: [[x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1]]` that leaves those cells air while the wall is built

waste.what: Checked the fit list for my footprint by grepping coordinate ranges with awk, because fit does not filter by part or footprint.
waste.cost: 2 grep passes
waste.tool: `mcd fit --box x0,z0,x1,z1` (or `--part`) to list only faults inside one part's cells

waste.what: Rendered tiles failed because the tiles directory did not exist.
waste.cost: 1 failed render
waste.tool: `mcd render --tiles` should create the directory itself

companions.task: Lay the strata courses by hand: the sandstone band table with the yellow_terracotta weathering, the orange band at y8, and the quoin-like breaks where the tiers meet, plus the ribbon slit reveal depth.
Set the dome drum, its saucer and the tier-top slab rings so the drum edge and the stairs meet with no half-block gap, and check the oculus seat over the atrium.
Fit the two dark oak door pairs in the east wall and the cut_sandstone jambs, and hang the porch lanterns from the lobe soffit at the right height.

summary:
NMAI grounds: NMAI grounds built in parts/nmai-grounds.mjs (423 blocks, no refusals, nothing off-palette): east plaza, pond with lily pads and sugar cane, four grandfather rocks, three birches, north dirt-path walk, podzol/coarse-dirt patches and meadow plants, a lamp-post lattice, plaza posts and base floodlights.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; fit reports OK; render shows the wetland and plaza where plan.md puts them. Shell is still a stub, so the tiers are not yet visible.
Plan moves recorded in plan.md Notes: B2 (128,14)->(128,15), birch (121,18)->(122,21), walk joins the plaza at x 134..135.
polish: E19 pond bed at y -1 and its two sea_lanterns are not built: the grid starts at y 0, so the pond is water at y 0 with no bed and the lanterns are dropped. elements.md E19 stays unticked.
The porch floor at y 1 (x 127..131, z 6..14) is left to the NMAI shell; the plaza skips those cells, so the shell must pave them.
Birch crowns at (95,15) and (113,22) may touch the T2 ring at about (96..97, 13..14); any refusals show only in the merged report.

Light is not complete: the NMAI footprint has no 0 cells, but several cells read 4 to 7 (below the 8 target) around the pond and the south-west tail. Lily pads show as orphans in `mcd check` (they sit on water with no solid base); this is harmless in game.
The NMAI tiers, lobes and dome are not in the build yet (the shell part is a stub), so the grounds have not been checked against the finished building in the render.

waste.what: Checked each plan coordinate against the ground map and the tier ellipses by hand, to find the boulder, birch and walk cells that collide with the porch or the T2 ring.
waste.cost: about 4 coordinate conflicts worked out by hand, plus one retry after a non-integer lattice x (Math.floor missed) that placed nothing
waste.tool: A `mcd plan`-style collision report for a part's footprint against earlier parts' ellipses (or a `--dry` on pond/boulder/birch that lists refused cells before writing) would have caught the conflicts at once.

waste.what: Lit the wetland by hand: a lattice of lamp posts 8 cells apart, then extra posts where the light map still read 0.
waste.cost: 3 build runs plus 2 light-map reads; the light map was the only check for the lattice
waste.tool: A `lattice(g, box, every, helper)` in vocab that places lamps only on free cells and reports the light gap, and `mcd light --y` printing the NMAI box only.

waste.what: Scattered meadow plants and podzol/coarse-dirt patches with a seeded random loop over every footprint cell and decided each cell's block by hand.
waste.cost: about 1 loop of 1,400 cells in one file, with rng thresholds tuned by eye
waste.tool: A `scatter(g, cells, {weights, seed})` helper that picks plants and patches by weight and skips taken cells.

waste.what: Ground surface writes (paths, podzol, plaza paving) at y = g, found cell by cell from the ground map.
waste.cost: about 400 cells with a per-cell lookup
waste.tool: A `surface(g, cells, block)` helper in base.mjs that reads the ground map and writes at the surface, so parts don't repeat the g lookup.

waste.what: `mcd light` with --rooms rooms.json printed only the header (no rooms), so I had to re-run with --y 1 and --y 2 to see the grounds.
waste.cost: 2 extra runs and a manual scan of the map
waste.tool: `mcd light` with no room listing should default to the whole build's floor level, or print a site map when rooms.json has none.

companions.task: Choose the wetland planting mix (reeds, sedges, podzol and coarse-dirt drifts) and lay out the north walk with its edges, so the meadow reads as native rather than random.
Light the wetland and the pond banks from a planned lamp grid, checking the light map so no cell is dark, and place the plaza and walk lamps so they read as one set.
Lay the four grandfather rocks as the rough tuff-andesite-granite mix they are, with the stone courses matching the strata of the museum.

summary: inspection: walk ok and fit OK, nothing to fix
